name: Mobile County
geoReference: Southwestern Alabama Gulf Coast bounded by Mobile Bay and the Mobile-Tensaw River Delta on the east, Mississippi Sound and the Gulf of Mexico on the south, and Mississippi on the west; served by I-10, I-65, I-165, US-90, US-98, US-43, US-45, AL-163, AL-188, and AL-193.
solidWasteNotes: City of Mobile biweekly 2 cu yd bulk trash rules and 3 resident-only recycling drop-off centers apply strictly inside Mobile corporate limits. Unincorporated Mobile County has no county curbside garbage or bulk collection (residents contract private haulers); Mobile County Commission operates the Hitt Rd Recycling Center (7450 Hitt Rd) and periodic Operation Clean Sweep events.

name: Baldwin County
geoReference: East of Mobile Bay across the I-10 Bayway and US-90/98 Causeway, stretching from the Mobile-Tensaw River Delta south to the Gulf of Mexico and east to the Perdido River/Florida line; served by I-10, I-65, US-31, US-90, US-98, AL-59, AL-104, AL-180, AL-181, AL-182, and the Baldwin/Foley Beach Express.
solidWasteNotes: The Solid Waste Disposal Authority of Baldwin County (SWDA) operates Magnolia Sanitary Landfill, the county MRF, C&D landfills, 3 CHaRM centers, and residential garbage/monthly bulk collection for unincorporated Baldwin County plus Bay Minette, Summerdale, Magnolia Springs, and Perdido Beach; the remaining 10 municipalities run independent public works or franchise sanitation programs.
